summary: Request for custom burst/refill policy to support occasional long-tail embedding spikes without impacting low-latency chat
description: BrightMaps is running a mixed workload on a Redwood Dedicated pool: low-latency chat for end-users and periodic large embedding backfills (long-tail documents). They are seeing unexpected 429s on embedding jobs during scheduled spikes which are degrading their bulk import SLA. They are requesting a nonstandard burst/refill policy (occasional high-capacity bursts without permanently increasing cost or harming chat latency) and guidance on configuration and migration steps.
impact: Bulk embedding jobs repeatedly receive 429s causing backfill to stretch past maintenance windows. Customer reports degraded analytics accuracy and missed deadlines. Chat latency (p95) occasionally increases when they tried naive workarounds.
environment: dedicated pool (arn:d:dedicated:pool/brightmaps-prod-3), prod: us-east primary with eu-west failover; Redwood console shows pool size 8 GPUs; autoscaler enabled; warmup policy default.
steps_to_reproduce: Schedule embedding backfill: 10k documents, batch size 512, concurrent workers 24
Target model: open-embed-xl (quantized), route to dedicated pool via api-key BRIGHT-PROD
Observe embedding tasks start around 02:00 UTC (customer's scheduled window)
Within 5-15 mins, embedding workers begin receiving 429 responses with Retry-After headers (range ~4-20s)
Customer attempts to reduce concurrency to 8; embedding still takes >maintenance window and intermittently receives 429s.
logs: 2026-03-12T02:09:02Z scheduler: queued batch 42 -> throttle triggered by tenant-window-exhaustion
comments: 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - Ava Chen (Support) - Initial intake: Customer requests a burst model that allows 3x sustained throughput for a 30 minute window once per day without changing long-term quotas. Wants to avoid separate pool due to cost. Asked for logs and exact schedule.

2026-03-12 10:15 UTC - Customer (BrightMaps - Ops) - Provided scheduling cron: 02:00 UTC daily for 4 hours, median document size 6KB, target 10k docs. Prefers not to maintain separate cluster if a config tweak can work.

2026-03-12 13:02 UTC - Liam O'Connor (SRE) - Triage: Reproduced token-window exhaustion in testenv when simulating 24 concurrent workers. Hypothesis: tenant-level burst credits exhausted quickly due to mixed realtime and bulk accounting sharing refill window. Suggested options: separate route quotas, create short-lived burst pool, or increase tenant burst credits temporarily.

2026-03-12 16:45 UTC - Priya Patel (Eng - Rate Limiter) - Added: We can support a scheduled burst policy via route_tags and scheduled_quota_refill; this requires config change and a short rollout. Need customer's approval for a temporary increase of refill rate during their window.
investigation_notes: Observed tenant token refill period = 60s with window size tied to tenant tier. Embedding request accounting counts tokens per document multiplied by batch size; large batches are depleting refill faster than expected.
Edge proxy connection reuse is stable; no duplicate accounting seen in request logs. Retry waves correlate with refill exhaustion rather than kernel saturation.
Dedicated pool autoscaler shows headroom but tenant token window prevents additional concurrent slots for this tenant during spike (throttle at software layer).
Simulated changes: increasing tenant refill_rate by 2.5x for 30 minutes removed 429s in test, but increased short-term cost metrics -- needs billing approval for recurring change.
resolution: (ongoing) Working with customer to choose path: 1) schedule a route-level temporary refill increase during their 02:00-06:00 UTC window using scheduled_quota_refill (recommended); 2) optionally create a dedicated burst route that maps to same pool but has isolated quota (higher admin cost). Action items: implement scheduled refill config, monitor cost delta for first two runs, update console to show scheduled quota in UI. Assigned SRE to create config and Eng to review billing impact.
